question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=3x(t)-{y}^{2}(t)+6y(t)-12 \\ {y}^{′}(t)={x}^{2}(t)+2x(t)+y(t)-6\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of ODEs above. An equilibrium point of the system is $[1,\,3]^{T}.$ Which of the following is the system obtained by shifting this equilibrium to the origin?
question.worked_solution:
To shift the system’s equilibrium from ${x}^{∗}$ to the origin, we define the deviation vector

$$
u=x-{x}^{∗},
$$

where

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}],\,u=[\begin{aligned}u(t) \\ v(t)\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
u=x-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\,⇒\,x=u+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\,\text{and}\,{x}^{′}={u}^{′}.
$$

In coordinate form, this can be written as follows:

$$
x(t)=u(t)+1,\,y(t)=v(t)+3,\,{x}^{′}(t)={u}^{′}(t),\,{v}^{′}(t)={y}^{′}(t).
$$

Let's now substitute these into the given system.

- Substituting into the first equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & =3x(t)-{y}^{2}(t)+6y(t)-12 \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =3(u(t)+1)-(v(t)+3)^{2}+6(v(t)+3)-12 \\  & =3u(t)+3-({v}^{2}(t)+6v(t)+9)+6v(t)+18-12 \\  & =3u(t)-{v}^{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

- Substituting into the second equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(t) & ={x}^{2}(t)+2x(t)+y(t)-6 \\ {v}^{′}(t) & =(u(t)+1)^{2}+2(u(t)+1)+(v(t)+3)-6 \\  & =({u}^{2}(t)+2u(t)+1)+2u(t)+2+v(t)+3-6 \\  & ={u}^{2}(t)+4u(t)+v(t).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the shifted system is the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{u}^{′}(t)=3u(t)-{v}^{2}(t) \\ {v}^{′}(t)={u}^{2}(t)+4u(t)+v(t)\end{aligned}
$$
